# System generation prompt: smart_camera

*Generated by ip/scripts/make_system_prompt.py on 2026-10-10. Edit any section before use.*

Create a complete FPGA / ASIC system for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library, built from the
existing library IP wherever possible.

## 1. Identity and goal

- Top module: `smart_camera`
- Location: `digital_ip/image_processing/smart_camera/`
- Purpose: Camera with lens correction, timestamp overlay, HDMI monitor out and UDP video streaming.
- Target: not selected (technology independent)

## 2. Features

- Control CPU with firmware
- Console / host UART
- I2C bus (sensors, EEPROM, PMIC, DDC)
- GPIO, LEDs, buttons
- MIPI CSI-2 camera input
- Lens distortion correction
- On-screen display / overlay
- DRAM frame buffer (frame-rate conversion)
- HDMI / DVI output
- Ethernet (UDP streaming / control)
- motion detection

## 3. External interfaces

| Interface | Standard / pins | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPI flash | SPI NOR: sclk, cs_n, mosi, miso | out/in | firmware image |
| UART | txd, rxd | out/in | 115200 8N1 default |
| I2C | scl, sda (open drain) | inout | - |
| GPIO | width TBD | inout | - |
| MIPI CSI-2 RX | 1-4 data lanes + clock lane (D-PHY) | in | RAW8/RAW10 |
| Camera control | I2C (CCI), reset, power-down GPIO | out | - |
| DDR | DDR3/DDR4/LPDDR, width TBD | inout | vendor controller |
| HDMI TX | 3 TMDS pairs + clock, DDC, HPD | out | - |
| Ethernet | RGMII / SGMII + MDIO | inout | - |



For every interface: the top-level ports, their clock, the `define that includes it, and which
module drives it. Analog / high-speed PHYs are vendor parts outside the technology-independent
top: expose their parallel (PPI / SerDes / PHY) interface as ports and document the board wrapper.

## 5. Functions not in the library and how to provide them

| Function | Needed by | Decision | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| MIPI D-PHY receiver (analog front end) | MIPI CSI-2 camera input | vendor | - |
| On-screen display / overlay (alpha blend, text, cursor) | On-screen display / overlay | new | AXI4-Stream video in/out, overlay plane from memory or a character ROM |
| DDR memory controller and PHY | DRAM frame buffer (frame-rate conversion) | vendor | vendor DDR3 controller, AXI4 128-bit |
| Video frame-buffer manager (triple buffering, frame-rate conversion) | DRAM frame buffer (frame-rate conversion) | new | writes frames with axis_dma, reads the newest complete frame for the display; register-programmed base addresses |
| Ethernet PHY (RGMII / SGMII) | Ethernet (UDP streaming / control) | vendor | - |
| UDP/IP offload (ARP, ICMP, UDP) | Ethernet (UDP streaming / control) | thirdparty | verilog-ethernet udp_complete (MIT) |
| Clock generation (PLL / MMCM) | video clocks | vendor | - |
| motion detection | user request | new | - |
| jpeg_encoder (named by the user, not in the library) | user request | stub | - |

- **MIPI D-PHY receiver (analog front end)** - use vendor IP behind a thin technology-independent wrapper (black box in synthesis, behavioural model in simulation)
- **On-screen display / overlay (alpha blend, text, cursor)** - create a new library module (use ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md for it): AXI4-Stream video in/out, overlay plane from memory or a character ROM
- **DDR memory controller and PHY** - use vendor IP behind a thin technology-independent wrapper (black box in synthesis, behavioural model in simulation): vendor DDR3 controller, AXI4 128-bit
- **Video frame-buffer manager (triple buffering, frame-rate conversion)** - create a new library module (use ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md for it): writes frames with axis_dma, reads the newest complete frame for the display; register-programmed base addresses
- **Ethernet PHY (RGMII / SGMII)** - use vendor IP behind a thin technology-independent wrapper (black box in synthesis, behavioural model in simulation)
- **UDP/IP offload (ARP, ICMP, UDP)** - use a third-party / open-source core (give its name and licence): verilog-ethernet udp_complete (MIT)
- **Clock generation (PLL / MMCM)** - use vendor IP behind a thin technology-independent wrapper (black box in synthesis, behavioural model in simulation)
- **motion detection** - create a new library module (use ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md for it)
- **jpeg_encoder (named by the user, not in the library)** - simulation stub only for now (same interface, behavioural model); the real block comes later

Rules: a **new** module follows ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md and is delivered with its own
testbench before it is integrated; **vendor** and **third-party** blocks sit behind a wrapper
with the interface stated above, are black boxes in synthesis, and get a behavioural model for
simulation; **stub** blocks have the real interface and a behavioural model only, listed as open
work in the report.

If, while designing, you find another function that is needed and not in the library (or not in
the tables above), stop and ask which option to use (new / vendor / third-party / stub / drop)
before continuing.

## 6. Architecture

- Data path: draw the chain from inputs to outputs using the module names above, with the stream
  format (width, tuser / tlast meaning) on every arrow and where each clock-domain crossing is.
- Control plane: one AXI4-Lite register space (py_soc (Python bytecode, boots from SPI flash)). Propose an address map
  (one window per block, in a table) and the interrupt list.
- Every optional block or interface is selected by a `define in `src/configuration.sv` (compiled
  first); excluded blocks have no ports or logic; a BUILD_CFG register reports what was built.
- Frame / packet boundaries: configuration changes take effect at the next frame or packet start.
- State explicitly where data can be dropped (rate mismatch, overflow), how it is counted, and how
  the system recovers without a reset.

## 7. Clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings and performance

- Clock domains: derive from the interfaces. List every domain, its frequency and source.
- Resets: one `reset_sync` per domain; reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.
- Video format: 1920x1080p60, 24-bit RGB
- Throughput / latency: real time, 1 pixel per clock, latency in lines not frames
- Timing target: pixel clock of the chosen video format; logic depth ~10
- Resource budget: none, report utilisation

## 8. Control processor and firmware

- Processor: py_soc (Python bytecode, boots from SPI flash)
- Firmware: start-up firmware that configures every block and reports status
- The firmware brings the system up the way a product would (release external devices from reset,
  configure them over I2C / SPI, program every block, enable interrupts, report status on a GPIO /
  UART) and checks for errors.

## 9. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent; vendor primitives only inside wrappers.
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (-g2012), Verilator lint (-Wall, no combinational loops or latches) and
  Yosys (sv2v where needed). Respect the iverilog limits: declare before use, no enum ternaries
  without casts, no `break`, no `wait` on functions, no queues in arrays, no declarations inside
  nested loops of static initial blocks.
- AXI4-Stream everywhere for data, AXI4-Lite for control; honour back-pressure, valid never depends
  on ready; a block that cannot be stalled must be documented and protected (FIFO, admission control).
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).

## 10. File header

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 11. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Tools

Use these tools for each step (the selection lives in `ip/.tools`; keep every script working with the default tools):

| Step | Tool | How it is run |
|------|------|---------------|
| Simulation | Icarus Verilog (`iverilog -g2012`, `vvp`) | `make test` / `scripts/run_sim.sh`; alternatives VCS, ModelSim, Questa (`SIMULATOR` in `ip/.tools`) |
| Python (cocotb) tests | cocotb on Verilator | `make python-test` (`PYTHON_SIMULATOR`) |
| Lint | Verilator (`--lint-only -Wall`) | `run_sim.sh --lint` (systems: `make lint`) |
| Waveform viewing | Surfer (VCD) | `make wave` / `run_sim.sh --wave` (`--vcd` only dumps) |
| Code coverage | Verilator `--coverage` + `verilator_coverage`, `ip/tools/cov/cov_report.py` | `make cov` / `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh` (LCOV `coverage.info`; vendor simulators: native coverage) |
| Formatting | `ip/scripts/sv_format.py` | `--check` before delivery |
| Synthesis | Yosys (Xilinx 7-series flow, sv2v where needed) | `make synth`; alternative Synplify (`SYNTHESIS`) |
| Place and route (optional) | Vivado | `PLACE_ROUTE` in `ip/.tools`, once a device is chosen |
| Diagrams | Graphviz (`dot`) | `make diagram` / `make diagrams` |
| Firmware (py_soc) | Python 3 + `ip/cpu/py_core/tools/pyc.py` | run by `scripts/run_sim.sh` |
| Test list | `ip/scripts/list_tests.py` | `run_sim.sh --list-tests` / `make list-tests` |
| Prompts and docs | `make_ip_prompts.py`, `gen_docs.py`, `make_block_diagrams.py` | regenerate after a change |


## 14. Verification

- A system testbench in `tb/` with board models (camera / link sources, display / link sinks that
  decode the real output, flash with the firmware image, I2C devices, ...).
- Nothing is programmed by the testbench if there is a CPU: the firmware boots and configures the system.
- End-to-end checks: every output compared with an independent reference model, pixel or byte exact
  (state any tolerance and why).
- Run the test in every interface configuration (`define on and off).
- Random gaps and back-pressure on internal streams where the models allow it.
- Mutation check: break one connection or setting and show the test fails.
- The library regressions of any IP you changed still pass.

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `scripts/run_sim.sh --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

| Test | Checks |
|------|--------|
| `test_<what>` | <one per requirement: boot, configuration, each interface, end-to-end data, error recovery, ...> |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

## 15. Report back

Summarise: the files created, the block, clock and reset diagrams, the address map, every change
to existing IP and why, the decisions taken for missing functions, the test list with results
(with the mutation check), coverage per metric (and every waiver), synthesis utilisation, and
the known limits and open work.
